prompt:
Here is a problem from another field that shares the underlying structure of the research question below, with notes on how that field investigates it.

<parallel>
Field: Geomechanics / rock physics
Problem: Do rocks and soils keep a record of the maximum stress they experienced in the past, and which microstructural feature holds that record?
How it is studied: In Kaiser-effect experiments, specimens are loaded to a known peak, unloaded, then reloaded while acoustic emissions are recorded. Emissions stay quiet until the previous peak is passed, and researchers measure how that onset fades with time delay, temperature, or water saturation. In soils, oedometer tests infer preconsolidation pressure from the break in the void-ratio vs. log-stress curve, and microCT links the memory to closed or newly formed microcracks.
</parallel>

Each of your ideas must transfer a specific method, measurement logic, or principle from how that field studies its problem, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the research question.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Kaiser-effect assay: graded re-stimulation after a known peak
ideas.description: Prime cells with a calibrated stimulus amplitude (e.g., serum, TGF-β, or stiffness), let signaling fully relax, then re-challenge parallel wells across a dose ladder spanning below and above the prime, reading out de novo AP-1 target transcription with live-cell FOS/JUN-family reporters and nascent-RNA (SLAM-seq) so that 'emission onset' is timed precisely. Memory is demonstrated if transcriptional response stays suppressed until the dose exceeds the prior peak and then rises sharply, with the breakpoint tracking the prime amplitude.

ideas.title: Decay-of-memory kinetics: delay, division number, and 'annealing' conditions
ideas.description: Repeat the prime/probe protocol while systematically varying the inter-stimulus interval, number of cell divisions (tracked by dye dilution or FUCCI sorting), and stressors analogous to temperature/saturation (HDAC or BRD4 inhibition, replication stress, osmotic chromatin decompaction), fitting the shift in re-activation threshold to an exponential or stretched-exponential decay. This yields a quantitative memory half-life and identifies which perturbations erase, accelerate, or protect the AP-1 record, distinguishing true storage from slow signal clearance.

ideas.title: Microstructural readout: latent AP-1 enhancers as the memory-bearing feature
ideas.description: Pair each mechanical-memory time point with ATAC-seq, AP-1 CUT&RUN, and H3K4me1/H3K27ac profiling to identify sites that open during the first exposure and remain open (or newly nucleosome-depleted) after signaling returns to baseline, exactly as microCT links preconsolidation memory to retained microcracks. Correlate the number and residual accessibility of these retained sites, site by site, with the measured re-activation threshold across priming doses.

ideas.title: Causal site-closure and site-opening test
ideas.description: Use dCas9-KRAB/DNMT3A to selectively re-close the retained AP-1 enhancers identified above, and dCas9-p300 or synthetic AP-1 tethering to pre-open them in naive cells, then re-run the graded re-stimulation assay. If these elements carry the record, closing them should abolish the threshold shift and opening them should install a false memory of an exposure that never occurred.

ideas.title: Single-cell preconsolidation inference and load-path discrimination
ideas.description: Treat each cell as a specimen: from single-cell multiome (ATAC+RNA) of cells with hidden exposure histories, fit the breakpoint in AP-1 target output versus log(stimulus dose) to infer a per-cell 'preconsolidation amplitude', then validate against the known true peak and test cell-to-cell spread. Contrast one large exposure against many sub-threshold cycles delivering equal cumulative dose to determine whether AP-1 records only the historical maximum or ratchets with cumulative loading.
